title: AI tool crm_set_conversation_sector moves any conversation in the organization, not only the conversation of the turn
description: In an AI turn driven by an untrusted WhatsApp sender, the in-process MCP bridge offers the model crm_set_conversation_sector with a free conversation_id. The sender can be a 1:1 customer or, since 0528, any member of a group where a manager enabled 'IA responde'. The handler checks only that the conversation belongs to the organization, then runs transferirParaSetor with the service-role client. That call silences the AI on the target conversation for good (bot_silenced_until='infinity', active_ai_agent_id=null), releases a human owner who is not in the sector, and re-routes the conversation. Nothing binds conversation_id to the turn's conversation or contact. The bridge passes the turn contact into ctx (turnContactId/contatoDoTurno), but this handler never reads it. guardServiceTools only re-checks the turn's own service boundary. The product binds every sibling path that has the same effect. The engine's request_human_handoff silences only the turn's conversation. The chatbot sector step uses its own conversation. The agenda tools refuse another contact's appointment through turnContactId, and the code documents the unbound case as a defect ('o contato A, conversando, levava a IA a cancelar ... o compromisso do contato B — com a identidade da organização'). The HTTP route requires RLS visibility plus exigirControleDaConversa. The same 'escalar' package also gives the model crm_list_conversations, which lists every conversation id in the organization with hidden ones included. So customer-controlled text can make the agent take other customers' conversations, private ones included, away from the AI and from their human owners and push them to a sector queue, using the organization's authority. The pre-existing crm_assign_conversation (same file, packages 'escalar' and 'atender') has the same org-only scoping.
root_cause: lib/mcp/tools/governance.ts:263-285 trusts the model-supplied conversation_id and scopes it only by ctx.organizationId before calling transferirParaSetor (lib/setores/servico.ts:125-217) with the service-role client. The AI-turn bridge (lib/ai/runtime/tools.ts wrapMcpTool) injects the turn contact into ctx, but it does not bind conversation selectors to the turn generically. This tool does not opt into the per-tool binding the agenda handlers use (exigeContatoDoTurno). guardServiceTools (lib/atendimento/fronteira-server.ts:138) validates only the current turn's own boundary, never the target.
intended_behavior: In a customer-driven conversation turn, the agent may move only THIS conversation to a sector. The tool's own description says 'você para de responder nesta conversa'. This matches the engine handoff, the chatbot step and the agenda rule 'A IA num turno de conversa só mexe no compromisso de QUEM está falando'. A conversation_id other than the turn's conversation must be refused, with no side effect.

trace.scope: inbound turn for a WhatsApp message (1:1 or AI-enabled group)
trace.description: The turn builds the catalog tools with buildMcpTurnTools, passing only organizationId, jobId and contactId (the turn contact). No conversation binding is passed.
pickToolsFromMcp gets role ai_operator (rank 3, above the tool's 'agent' floor), mcp:write scope, the service-role client cfg.supabase, and turnContactId/contatoDoTurno.
Lists the organization's conversations with ocultas 'incluir' and returns their ids, which gives the model target ids belonging to other customers.
After the scope/role checks and the funnel gate (the tool is 'sem_funil', so it is allowed), the handler is called with the model's arguments unchanged.
The only per-effect guard checks that the turn's OWN boundary (its conversation) is still current. It never checks the target conversation.
Calls transferirParaSetor with input.conversation_id and only the organization from ctx.

The service-role UPDATE on the chosen conversation sets setor_id, bot_silenced_until='infinity' and last_handoff_reason='setor', and clears active_ai_agent_id. It then releases the owner via fn_conversation_assign (line 201) and re-routes via fn_request_channel_routing (line 213).

evidence.description: conversation_id is any UUID. No relation to the turn is required.
Comment states that only the organization is trusted: 'a organização vem do contexto confiável, e a conversa e o setor são conferidos dentro dela'.
The tool description given to the model promises the effect applies to 'nesta conversa'.
The tool is offered in the 'escalar' package.
crm_list_conversations is in the same 'escalar' package (crm_get_conversation too, line 95).
The tool is declared sem_funil, so the bridge's only target gate allows it unconditionally.
The engine's MCP client is created with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, so RLS on conversations does not apply.

Sibling control and stated threat model: in an AI turn, writes to another contact's appointment are refused (exigeContatoDoTurno, line 253). The comment describes contact A driving the AI to act on contact B's object as a defect.
Sibling: the engine handoff applies the same silence effect only to ids.conversationId of the turn.
Sibling: the human route requires RLS visibility (line 58) and exigirControleDaConversa before the same transfer.
Sibling: the chatbot sector step uses its own conversation id.
The pre-existing crm_assign_conversation also scopes the model-supplied conversation_id only by organization before the service-role fn_conversation_assign. Same missing binding.

conditions.description: None. Any WhatsApp number that can message the organization's connected channel, or any member of a group where a manager turned on 'IA responde'.

The organization's published agent has crm_set_conversation_sector (the 'escalar' package, or the tool chosen individually), and at least one sector exists. For target ids: crm_list_conversations or crm_get_conversation from the same package, or any other source of a conversation UUID.
The LLM follows customer-supplied instructions and calls the tool with another conversation_id. Model output is untrusted by design. Model compliance was not exercised locally.
The target conversation exists in the same organization. It may be private or owned by an attendant.

execution.attacker_perspective: A WhatsApp sender with no CRM account, whose messages drive an AI turn of the organization's published agent.
payloads: crm_set_conversation_sector {"conversation_id":"c0000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000b2","setor":"Financeiro"} executed inside an inbound_turn whose service boundary is contact c0000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000a1 / conversation c0000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000b1

instructions: This is the verifier's own bounded harness, written independently of the hunter's artifact. Build the tool the way the engine turn does: pickToolsFromMcp({toolIds:['crm_set_conversation_sector'], ctx:{organizationId:O, role:'ai_operator', actor ai_agent, turnContactId:T}, contatoDoTurno:T, scopes mcp:read/mcp:write, pipelineIds:[], modulosLigados:[], capacidadesLigadas:[]}). Back it with a recording in-memory Supabase double holding the turn conversation CT (contact T), a victim conversation CV (contact V, is_private=true, assigned to a human), a conversation CX in another org, and sector 'Financeiro'.

Wrap the tools with guardServiceTools and execute inside withServiceJob(inbound_turn, boundary org O / contact T / conversation CT, revision 7), with a boundary reader that returns the current revision for CT.
Call execute({conversation_id: CV, setor: 'Financeiro'}). Controls: the same call with CX (another org), and with CT (the turn's own conversation).
Run inside sb verifier-conversa (no network, read-only repository, scratch-only writes): vitest run --config ./vitest.verif.config.mjs --reporter=verbose.
execution.observed_result: From agents/verifier-conversa/artifacts/evidence/turno-setor.log, 3/3 passed, exit=0, with details in agents/verifier-conversa/artifacts/evidence/turno-setor-result.json. With a current boundary for conversation CT, the call on the victim conversation CV returned {conversation_id: CV, setor_id: <Financeiro>, setor: 'Financeiro', setor_anterior_id: null}. It issued UPDATE conversations SET setor_id=<Financeiro>, bot_silenced_until='infinity', last_handoff_reason='setor', active_ai_agent_id=null, active_intent=null WHERE organization_id=O AND id=CV, then rpc fn_conversation_assign(p_conversation_id=CV, p_to_user_id=null, p_reason='release'), then rpc fn_request_channel_routing(CV). Conversation CT was unchanged. Control CX (other org): the bridge returned {error: 'conversa_nao_encontrada'} with zero effects, which shows the organization filter is the only check. Control CT: the turn's own conversation is handled exactly like the victim's. The RPCs are recorded by the double, not executed. The effect of the service-role release on a real baseline (owner unassigned and losing sight) was observed separately in agents/verifier-conversa/artifacts/evidence/convidado-controle.log, case V3.

remediation.strategy: Bind the target to the turn. When ctx.actor.type is 'ai_agent' and the call comes from a customer-driven turn (a current execution boundary or a turnContactId exists), accept only the conversation of currentExecutionBoundary(). Without a boundary, require conversations.contact_id === ctx.turnContactId. Otherwise return a refusal the model can read, with no side effect. Calls with no turn context keep today's behavior. Preferably enforce this once in wrapMcpTool for every write tool whose arguments carry conversation_id or contact_id, and cover crm_assign_conversation and crm_manage_tags the same way. Regression test: calling with another conversation returns the refusal and records no UPDATE or RPC, while calling with the turn's conversation still succeeds.

likelihood.reason: It needs the 'escalar' package (or this tool) enabled, sectors configured, and a model that obeys injected customer text. The attacker needs no account, and target ids are easy to obtain because crm_list_conversations ships in the same package.

impact.reason: This affects the integrity and availability of other customers' service across the organization. Their conversations, private ones included, can be silenced for the AI with no expiry, taken from their human owner and pushed to a sector queue, and repeated calls scale to every listed conversation. The tool itself discloses no data, and there is no cross-tenant effect.

confidence.reason: The real bridge, turn guard, handler and transfer service ran in the sandbox and acted on a conversation outside the turn. The other-org control shows the organization filter is the only check. The only stand-in is the PostgREST client double, which records the exact filters, patch and RPCs the code sends. LLM compliance is a stated condition and is reflected in the likelihood. It is not an uncertainty about the missing binding.

title: System update/rollback/force dispatch accepts read-only-scope platform admins and password-only (aal1) sessions of admins with an enrolled MFA factor
description: POST /api/v1/system/update is the endpoint behind "Atualizar agora", "Voltar para a versão anterior" and "Forçar atualização". It writes a dispatched system_update_runs row through the service-role client. On its next 5-minute cron, the host update agent executes that row as update.sh. update.sh takes a backup, puts up the maintenance page, re-applies the baseline, swaps images and restarts; for rollback and force it adds --force. The only authorization the route performs is user.is_platform_admin. That flag is true for any non-revoked platform_admins row, whatever its scope and whatever the session's assurance level. As a result, a platform admin with scope 'support_readonly' can dispatch an update, a rollback or a forced re-run. So can anyone who holds only the password of a platform admin who enrolled TOTP, from an aal1 session that never passed the second factor. Every sibling instance-write path refuses the same principals: the extension install/update/remove guard, escritaDeAdminOuRecusa/requirePlatformAdmin, the platform shortcut in requireRole, and the DB rule fn_support_write_allowed. The documented contract (docs/specs/01-spec-platform-base.md:182) says that platform_admins.scope sets the maximum authority and that anyone with a verified factor must prove aal2 on protected routes. Calibration against the comparable baseline: upstream release v1.116.0, whose tag is present in this clone, gates this same route with requirePlatformAdminEscrita() (scope='full' plus strict MFA), with the comment 'support_readonly e sessão com dívida de MFA não disparam'. The fork's port omitted that guard. lib/auth/recusa-de-escrita-de-admin.ts:5 still names requirePlatformAdminEscrita, which does not exist in the fork.
root_cause: app/api/v1/system/update/route.ts:57 gates only on user.is_platform_admin. lib/auth/server.ts:273 derives that flag as !!paRow from a platform_admins read that selects only user_id and revoked_at (server.ts:178), so scope is never consulted. The route never calls sessionAal() or mfaEmDivida() and never reads mfa_required. proxy.ts applies its platform check only to /admin paths (proxy.ts:180), and it has no MFA step-up for /api. The route then writes through createAdminClient (route.ts:61). The service role bypasses the DB-side rule fn_support_write_allowed (migration 0501), which would refuse scope<>'full' or mfa_required without aal2.
intended_behavior: Dispatching a host-affecting update, rollback or forced re-run should require platform_admins.scope='full'. It should also require aal2 whenever platform_admins.mfa_required is true or the user has a verified factor (mfaEmDivida()), and it should refuse an active support session. That is what requireExtensionPlatformFor (lib/extensions/http.ts:70,80) and escritaDeAdminOuRecusa enforce for other instance-level writes, and what upstream's requirePlatformAdminEscrita enforces on this same route. A support_readonly admin should get 403 forbidden, and a password-only aal1 session of an admin with a factor should get 403 mfa_required, with no system_update_runs row created.

trace.description: Cookie-session POST. The body selects the order: {} (update), {rollback:true} or {force:true}.
requireSupportWrite() only refuses an active read-only support SESSION. For a platform admin outside support mode it returns null.
The platform_admins read selects only user_id and revoked_at. Neither scope nor mfa_required is read, and no assurance level is computed.
is_platform_admin = !!paRow, so it is true for a support_readonly row and for any session level.
The only authorization gate is is_platform_admin. There is no scope='full' check and no aal2/mfaEmDivida check.
Service-role insert of {status:'dispatched', to_version: alvo}. alvo is latest for an update, or v<from_version> of the last failed run for rollback and force (lines 137, 180, 237).
The next host heartbeat receives update_requested:true and the run's to_version.
The host agent cron runs update.sh --to <alvo>, adding --force for older targets (backup, maintenance pause, baseline re-apply, image swap/restart or downgrade).

evidence.description: The sibling instance-level guard (extension install/update/remove) refuses platform.scope !== 'full'.
The same guard requires aal2 when mfa_required is set, or whenever mfaEmDivida() (a verified factor in an aal1 session) applies.
Platform-write helper used by server actions in this diff: it returns forbidden_scope unless scope is 'full', after requirePlatformAdmin's MFA check.
The platform admin surface requires aal2 when mfa_required is set or a TOTP factor is verified.
The platform-admin shortcut in requireRole refuses sessions for which mfaEmDivida() is true.
The installed fn_support_write_allowed (0501, the last definition) denies platform writes when scope<>'full' or when mfa_required is set without aal2. The service-role route never reaches this rule.
The platform_admins.scope CHECK admits 'support_readonly' as a defined read-only platform scope.
Contract: platform_admins defines maximum authority and scope, and anyone who has a verified factor must prove aal2 on protected routes.
Names requirePlatformAdminEscrita, the upstream instance-write guard that upstream v1.116.0 applies to this route. The guard is absent from the fork, which shows that the port dropped it.
The global proxy's platform check covers only /admin paths. Nothing adds an MFA step-up for /api/v1/system/update.

conditions.description: A platform_admins row with scope='support_readonly' (read-only support staff provisioned by the DBA), or a full-scope platform admin whose credentials are partially compromised.
For the full-scope case: an aal1 (password-only) session of an admin who has a verified TOTP factor or mfa_required=true, for example a stolen password before the MFA challenge.

Rollback and force require the latest run to be failed or failed_rolled_back. A plain update requires latest_version != current_version. A dispatched run older than 15 minutes is expired and replaced; a fresher one blocks with 409.
The host update agent cron is installed (setup_update_agent_cron, every 5 minutes).

execution.attacker_perspective: A platform administrator whose platform_admins row has scope 'support_readonly', or anyone holding only the password of a platform admin with an enrolled TOTP factor (session at aal1), calling the API directly with that session cookie.

instructions: Verifier's own reproduction (not the hunter's harness). Inside the parent sandbox (no network), run vitest on harness/verif-update.test.ts (copied to evidence/system-update-verif-harness.txt). It imports the real route, lib/auth/server.ts, lib/impersonate/support.ts, lib/extensions/http.ts, lib/auth/escritaDeAdminOuRecusa.ts and requirePlatformAdmin.ts. Only the two Supabase clients (backed by one in-memory store), next/headers, next/navigation, audit, logger and env are faked.

For each of P1, P2 and P3, record mfaEmDivida(), requireExtensionPlatform() and escritaDeAdminOuRecusa(). Then call the real POST with {} (system_version current 1.1.0, latest 1.2.0), and with {rollback:true} and {force:true} (last run status 'failed', from_version '1.0.0'). Record the HTTP status and the dispatched system_update_runs row.
Controls: a user with no platform_admins row must get 403, and a full-scope aal2 admin must be accepted by both requireExtensionPlatform and the route.

In a throwaway Postgres 16 with baseline.sql applied (sb --pg), run evidence/platform-scope-verif.sql. It inserts a support_readonly admin (mfa_required=true) and a full admin, then executes loadAuthUser's exact platform_admins read as role authenticated with aal1 claims, and compares fn_is_platform_admin() with fn_support_write_allowed().
execution.observed_result: Verifier's bounded reproduction (evidence/system-update-verif.log, evidence/platform-scope-verif.log). P1 (support_readonly, aal1, TOTP): mfaEmDivida()=true; requireExtensionPlatform returned 403 forbidden; escritaDeAdminOuRecusa redirected to /login/mfa. The update route still returned 200 for {} and inserted {from_version:'1.1.0', to_version:'1.2.0', status:'dispatched'}. It returned 200 for {rollback:true} and for {force:true}, each inserting a dispatched run to 'v1.0.0'. P2 (support_readonly, aal2): requireExtensionPlatform returned 403 forbidden and escritaDeAdminOuRecusa returned {ok:false, error:'forbidden_scope'}, but all three route calls returned 200 with dispatched rows. P3 (full scope, password-only aal1 with a verified TOTP): requireExtensionPlatform returned 403 mfa_required, but all three route calls returned 200 with dispatched rows. In the controls, the non-admin got 403 with no row, and the full-scope aal2 admin got {ok:true} and 200. In Postgres, as authenticated with aal1 claims, the support_readonly user's loadAuthUser read returned its own row (scope support_readonly, mfa_required t). fn_is_platform_admin() was t, while fn_support_write_allowed(org) was f. The full admin at aal1 also resolved fn_is_platform_admin()=t. The installed fn_is_platform_admin has no scope filter, and platform_admins_self is the only policy.

remediation.strategy: Gate the route with the instance-write guard: refuse an active support session, require platform_admins.scope='full', and require aal2 when mfa_required is set or mfaEmDivida() is true. The cleanest fix is to port upstream's requirePlatformAdminEscrita/falhaDaEscritaDePlatformAdmin (which recusa-de-escrita-de-admin.ts already expects) and call it here, so that extensions, server actions and system update share one guard. Add regression cases: support_readonly gets 403 and no row; a full-scope aal1 session with a verified factor gets 403 mfa_required and no row; a full-scope aal2 session gets 200.

likelihood.reason: Requires a platform-admin principal: either the DBA-provisioned support_readonly scope or the password of a full-scope admin who enrolled a factor, without the second factor. Tenant users and anonymous callers cannot reach it.

impact.reason: Bypasses both the read-only scope and the MFA step-up for the only app path that triggers a root-run host operation. The host agent then takes a backup, raises the maintenance pause, re-applies the baseline and swaps images, or after a failed run performs a forced rollback or re-run. The impact is on the availability and version integrity of the whole installation. The attacker cannot choose an arbitrary target through this route alone (it is derived from latest_version or the failed run's from_version), and there is no direct data disclosure.

confidence.reason: Every trace line was re-read in source. An independent bounded harness ran the real route and sibling guards for three principals plus controls, and a throwaway Postgres confirmed that a support_readonly admin resolves as is_platform_admin while the DB rule refuses it. Upstream v1.116.0 applies exactly the missing guard to this route.

title: A marketing refusal recorded as {granted:false} stops prospecting but not automations or campaigns
description: The fork's declared single refusal rule recusaRegistrada (lib/lgpd/recusa-registrada.ts) treats consent.marketing.declined_at or granted === false as a recorded refusal. Its header says that the contact card's PATCH writes the {granted:false} shape and that the automation, e-mail, campaign and prospecting guards all call the helper. In this fork only prospecting does: motivoDoVetoDoContato and the prospecting export. The automation guard checarGuardasDeContato (send_whatsapp_message, send_ai_message, start_chatbot_flow) and the campaign rule recusouMarketing, used at audience preparation, the test send and every round's send-time revalidation, still read only declined_at. The fork's own tracking doc lists upstream commit 9460d627a ('a recusa gravada pela ficha (granted: false) bloqueia o envio') as not yet ported. The contacts POST and PATCH (agent or higher, session) accept consent as any record and merge it per purpose, so {marketing:{granted:false}} is writable. Once written, prospecting stops but template and AI automations and campaign rounds keep sending marketing to that person. The LGPD PDF labels that purpose 'negado', although it uses the same label for never-asked contacts. Scope note from verification: no UI in this fork writes the granted:false-only shape. The 'não tenho interesse' classifier writes both granted:false and declined_at, and the Respondi webhook writes declined_at. The trigger is therefore an API or direct-table write, or data carried over from upstream. Verified by the verifier's own sandboxed run (agents/verifier-onda2/artifacts/evidence/automation-marks-repro.log).
root_cause: lib/automation/guarda-do-contato.ts:87 and lib/campanhas/elegibilidade.ts:171-175 read consent.marketing.declined_at directly instead of calling recusaRegistrada (lib/lgpd/recusa-registrada.ts:21-27). The upstream change that routed every sender through the helper was ported only for the prospecting guard and export.
intended_behavior: A recorded marketing refusal, in either shape the product's own rule recognizes, blocks every marketing sender: automation, campaign and prospecting. The helper's header states that all of these guards call it.

trace.description: An agent-or-higher session updates a contact; contactPatchSchema (derived from contactCreateSchema, lib/schemas/contacts.ts:60/78) accepts consent as any record
Consent is merged per purpose, storing consent.marketing = {granted:false} without declined_at
The refusal check reads only declined_at, so {granted:false} passes
The campaign refusal check reads only declined_at; it is used at preparation (consulta-de-audiencia.ts:132), in the test send (acoes.ts:423) and at send time (rodada.ts:279)
The marketing template is sent through sendMessageHandler; the campaign round sends at lib/campanhas/rodada.ts:456

evidence.description: Source-of-truth rule: declined_at or granted === false is a refusal
Header states that reading only declined_at let refusals made from the contact card through to automation, e-mail, campaign and prospecting, and that all four guards call this helper
Prospecting enforces recusaRegistrada, so the same contact is vetoed there and nowhere else
Upstream fix 9460d627a ('a recusa gravada pela ficha (granted: false) bloqueia o envio') is listed as not yet ported
consent: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()) lets POST and PATCH store the granted:false shape
The LGPD export renders a purpose with granted false as 'negado' (it does not distinguish refusal from never-asked)

conditions.description: An agent-or-higher session records the refusal as {marketing:{granted:false}} through the contacts POST or PATCH API, or by a direct table update. No UI in this fork writes that shape alone.
An automation rule with a send action, or a campaign, targets the contact.

execution.attacker_perspective: This is a compliance boundary rather than an attacker gain. The organization's later automatic jobs ignore a marketing refusal that the organization itself recorded in a shape its own refusal rule recognizes.

control consent = {"marketing":{"granted_at":null,"declined_at":"2026-11-01T00:00:00Z"}, ...}

The real recusaRegistrada, motivoDoVetoDoContato, checarGuardasDeContato, recusouMarketing and the send_whatsapp_message body run on a dummy contact; only the sink and non-consent dependencies are mocked.
Compare against the declined_at control.

In the declined_at control, the guard returned consent_declined and recusouMarketing returned true. send_whatsapp_message with the granted:false contact returned status success with sink calls = 1.

remediation.strategy: Route every marketing-refusal read through recusaRegistrada. Replace the declined_at reads in guarda-do-contato.ts and campanhas/elegibilidade.ts, and add regression cases with {granted:false} for the automation guard, campaign preparation and the send-time round.

impact.reason: Marketing messages reach a person whose refusal the organization recorded, which is an LGPD consent-enforcement gap. No data disclosure and no cross-tenant effect.

title: Any tenant member, even a viewer, can forge appointment events that make the org's WhatsApp number send spoofed appointment notices, suppress real ones, and use up the number's shared daily send cap
description: Migration 0551 adds an event_log consumer (agenda-aviso-no-whatsapp.v1). It turns every pending appointment.created, appointment.rescheduled and appointment.cancelled row into a WhatsApp message sent from the organization's connected number to the configured owner phone. These three types are not reserved in the installed public.emit_event. That function is SECURITY DEFINER, EXECUTE is granted to authenticated, it only requires viewer membership, and it records no actor. The consumer trusts the row. It takes the appointment id and the origin label (payload.autor) from the caller-chosen payload. It checks only that the appointment exists and, for created/rescheduled, that it is pending or confirmed. It claims one delivery per event_log id. A viewer cannot create, reschedule or cancel appointments (fn_appointment_change_core requires agent) and cannot configure or test the notice (admin-only). Yet a viewer can do three things. (a) Make the owner receive 'agendamento cancelado ... Origem: Cliente' for an appointment that is still confirmed, which invites a double booking. (b) Cancel a real notice that is still held (spacing or cap deferral, or night hold) for the same appointment, so the real notice is never sent. (c) Emit one row per message to use up the number's daily send cap in pacing_ledger. That cap is the lower of the warm-up step (20 per day for a number without a channel_knobs row) and channel_sessions.daily_message_limit (default 300). AI-agent replies and campaigns read the same ledger and the same cap, so for the rest of that local day they are vetoed and rescheduled to the next day's sending window (07:00 local by default). title: 0540 contact marks (is_personal / ai_opt_out / force_human) stay on the card when the person's WhatsApp number and lid leave it through a merge, agent phone edits or an agent deleting the card
description: Migration 0540 adds two manager-only vetoes on the contact row: is_personal (nothing automatic goes out to the contact) and ai_opt_out (the AI never answers, it also sets force_human, and no handback undoes it). Both are stored and evaluated per contact card id. In the same diff, migration 0541 adds ways to move a person's WhatsApp identity (the number plus the WhatsApp lid that inbound resolution uses) from one card to another, and none of them reads or carries the marks. (1) Agent-role phone routes: add an extra to the marked card, promote it to principal (fn_tornar_telefone_principal strips waha_lid from the principal and re-inserts the old number with its lid as an extra), delete that extra, and add the freed number to another, unmarked card. The agent-role PATCH /contacts/{id} reaches the same result by rewriting phone_number and source_metadata. (2) The manager merge fn_mesclar_contatos: the absorbed card's conversations, lid and principal number go to the survivor (steps 5, 6 and 6b), but the survivor update never ORs in the absorbed card's marks. (3) The agent-role DELETE /contacts/{id} (deleteContactHandler) deletes the marked card itself, after removing its messages and conversations through the admin client, without reading the marks; the person's next inbound then creates a fresh unmarked card. This takes one call but visibly erases the conversation history. Every veto consumer (before-send readStopFlags, AI eligibility in consulta-pg / consulta-supabase, prospecting and campaign guards) reads only the card the conversation or inbound resolves to, so once the identity has moved or the card is gone, the marked person's next inbound and existing conversation are evaluated against an unmarked card. Today an agent can already clear the marks directly, because the column guard fn_contato_colunas_de_controle does not cover them (a separate finding). This root cause is independent: it survives a fix of that guard, and it fails open silently on a routine manager merge, with no audit row for the lost veto.
root_cause: The 0540 marks live only on public.contacts rows and are evaluated per card id, while the card-level operations that move or drop the person's identity treat the number and lid as freely movable card attributes and never union, copy or check the marks: the survivor update and step 6b of fn_mesclar_contatos (installed definition, baseline.sql:45766 and 45833), fn_tornar_telefone_principal (baseline.sql:46452), the agent-floor contact_phones add/delete handlers (app/api/v1/contacts/[id]/phones/_handler.ts:175, :245, :296), whose only card check fichaViva (:103) reads id and phone_number, and the agent-floor contact delete (app/api/v1/contacts/_handler.ts:917, RLS policy contacts_delete_de_atendente at baseline.sql:50503). fn_upsert_wa_contact (baseline.sql:45304) then resolves the person's next inbound to whichever live card holds the number or lid, or creates a new card.
intended_behavior: A veto attached to a person must keep applying to that person's WhatsApp number and lid wherever they end up. A merge should OR the absorbed cards' is_personal, ai_opt_out and force_human into the survivor (fail closed, as the function already does for consent). Detaching a number or lid from a card that carries a manager-only mark, or deleting such a card, should require at least the manager role, or the mark should be kept with the identity rather than only on the card.

title: Agent who cannot view a conversation can attach their own WhatsApp number to the customer's record and receive that conversation's outbound messages
description: Conversation visibility is an authorization boundary enforced in the database. conversations_select and messages_select apply fn_can_view_conversation and the sector scope from 0543, and fn_conversation_assign refuses to let a caller take over a conversation they cannot view (0499). In the default visibility_mode own_and_unassigned, an agent cannot see conversations assigned to colleagues. In own_and_sector, an agent cannot see other sectors' conversations, and in every mode private conversations are hidden. Contacts, however, are readable org-wide, and POST /api/v1/contacts/{id}/phones (and promotion via /primary) requires only role agent. The extra number becomes an inbound identity of the contact: fn_upsert_wa_contact falls through to contact_phones. It also becomes the reply destination of every WAHA conversation of that contact, because chatIdDaUltimaRecebida returns the last inbound chat as soon as the contact has any extra and that chat matches an extra. The attack: an agent attaches a WhatsApp number they control to customer Y and sends one message from it. The message is filed into Y's existing hidden conversation. Every outbound of that conversation is then addressed to the agent's chat until Y writes again. That covers the AI reply to the injected message, follow-ups, scheduled and automation sends through sendMessageHandler, the watchdog redrive and replies from the colleague who owns the conversation. The agent's messages also appear in Y's thread as if Y wrote them. Comparable pattern: PATCH /contacts/{id} lets an agent change the principal number, which redirects only contacts without a wa_lid. The extra-phone path redirects lid contacts too.
root_cause: Phone writes for a contact are authorized only by org membership and role >= agent. The route calls requireRole('agent') and the RLS policy tenant_isolation_contact_phones_write applies fn_role_at_least(org,'agent'), with no relation to conversation visibility. The written number is nevertheless trusted downstream as the customer's identity. It drives inbound matching (fn_upsert_wa_contact through contact_phones, then fn_upsert_wa_conversation returning the existing 1:1 conversation) and reply routing (chatIdDaUltimaRecebida, then resolveWahaChatId, where ultimoRecebidoChatId wins over the contact's wa_lid and phone). Both apply to every conversation of the contact, including conversations the writer may not view.
intended_behavior: An agent who cannot view a contact's conversations must not be able to redirect those conversations' outbound messages or inject inbound messages into them as the customer. Adding, editing the WhatsApp flag of or promoting a phone should require that the caller can view every conversation of the contact, or a manager role. This is the same rule fn_conversation_assign already applies to takeovers. Alternatively, a manually added extra should not become a reply destination until someone who can view the conversation confirms it.

ultimoRecebidoChatId takes precedence over the contact's own wa_lid and phone. wahaAdapter.resolveRecipient delegates here.

title: Contacts CSV export writes outsider-controlled names as live spreadsheet formulas
description:
GET /api/v1/contacts/export?formato=csv (manager) builds the file with csvDosContatos and linhaDoCsv. These pass name and display_name through csvEscape, which applies only RFC 4180 quoting. Unauthenticated outsiders can set both fields:
- name: from the public lead-capture webhook /api/v1/webhooks/in/[token]. Its signing secret is optional, and the webhook is usually embedded in a website form.
- display_name: the WhatsApp push name of anyone who messages the business number, stored by fn_upsert_wa_contact.

A name that starts with =, +, -, @, TAB or CR reaches the downloaded .csv unchanged. The file is prepared for Excel in Portuguese (it carries a BOM), so the cell becomes an active formula when a manager opens it. A HYPERLINK formula can then send other cells of the exported base, such as phone numbers and e-mails, to an attacker host when clicked.

The repository's own rule disagrees with this exporter. lib/exportacao/csv.ts and lib/prospecting/exportar.ts prefix ' to such cells while keeping E.164 phones intact. The prospecting exporter even calls this 'a mesma regra do export de contatos', but the contacts exporter does not implement it.

Reproduced locally. The exporter wrote =1+1 and =HYPERLINK(...&D3,"Ver") unchanged. LibreOffice Calc 24.2 imported that file with A2 as the formula 1+1 evaluated to 2, and A3 as a live HYPERLINK formula. The same names passed through the repository's neutralizer imported as plain text.
root_cause: csvEscape in lib/contacts/exportar.ts (lines 65-69) applies only RFC 4180 quoting. It omits the formula-prefix neutralization that the repository's other CSV exporters apply (pareceFormula/celula in lib/exportacao/csv.ts, neutralizarFormula in lib/prospecting/exportar.ts). Outsider-controlled name and display_name values are therefore written verbatim as formula cells.
intended_behavior: Every exported cell that starts with =, +, -, @, TAB or CR is prefixed with ' before quoting unless the whole value is a phone number (the TELEFONE_FORMATADO exemption that lib/prospecting/exportar.ts applies and calls 'a mesma regra do export de contatos'), so that no imported value becomes an active formula. E.164 phone numbers stay intact.

trace.description: An anonymous form submission (path token only; the signing secret is optional, line 161) maps the payload into contacts.name (`name: mapped.name ?? mapped.phone`) with no formula neutralization.
This is a second outsider writer. The WhatsApp push name becomes p_notify and is stored in contacts.display_name by the last definition of fn_upsert_wa_contact (supabase/baseline.sql:45430).
The manager export reads the organization's contacts with listContactsHandler and maps name and display_name into ContatoParaExportar (lines 174-181).
For formato=csv, the body is csvDosContatos(contatos), served as a text/csv attachment (lines 208-216).
Each field goes through csvEscape and nothing else.
csvEscape quotes the value only when it contains a quote, comma or newline. A leading = + - @ stays in place, so the cell becomes a live formula in the spreadsheet application.

evidence.description: The shared exporter neutralizes formula-looking cells (`if (pareceFormula(texto)) texto = `'${texto}``). Its header (lines 8-15) states the threat: customer-written text that starts with = becomes a formula on the owner's computer.
The sibling exporter documents formula neutralization as 'a mesma regra do export de contatos (lib/contacts/exportar.ts)', a rule the contacts exporter does not implement.
The CSV gets a BOM specifically for Excel in Portuguese, so the intended consumer is a spreadsheet application.
csvEscape applies RFC 4180 quoting only and never checks the leading character.
The source secret is 'defesa opcional', so a website form can post names with only the path token.
fn_upsert_wa_contact (last definition) inserts nullif(p_notify,'') into contacts.display_name.

title: Contacts import email check runs in quadratic time, so one crafted upload by any agent stalls the shared app process
description:
POST /api/v1/contacts/import requires the agent role. It accepts a CSV or vCard of up to 5 MiB and passes each data row to mapLinha. mapLinha caps name and display_name at 200 characters, but it tests the full email cell against /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ before any length check or Zod schema. On the cell 'a@' followed by N dots and a final '@', V8's backtracking engine does O(N^2) work: every split point of the second [^\s@]+ re-scans the rest of the dots before $ fails. The call is synchronous, inside the request handler.

Measured locally on the route's own pure sequence (decodificarCsv, parseCsv, mapHeader, mapLinha):
- Timings were 5 ms at 2.5 KB, 20 ms at 5 KB, 60 ms at 10 KB, 251 ms at 20 KB and 1,051 ms at 40 KB, about 4x per doubling.
- A 10 ms timer queued in the same process fired only after the 40 KB call returned, 1,230 ms later.
- Extrapolated, not run: about 12 minutes for a 1 MiB cell and about 5 hours at the 5 MiB cap.
- The vCard path reaches the same regex with EMAIL capped at 20,000 characters per logical line, at about 0.3 s per card.

The shipped production topology is one app container running a single `node server.js` process, which serves every organization's UI, API and incoming webhooks. Nothing source-visible bounds the request below the app's 5 MiB cap: Caddy's reverse_proxy has no body limit, the route has no rate limit, and Next.js buffers proxy bodies up to 10 MiB. The healthcheck is a raw TCP connect, and restart: unless-stopped does not restart a blocked process, so recovery is a manual restart. The regex predates the diff (blame 823812681), but it is on the assigned import path.
root_cause: mapLinha (lib/contacts/csv.ts:411-413) runs an ambiguous backtracking regex on an uncapped, user-supplied email cell. Validation is therefore quadratic in a cell length that only the 5 MiB file cap bounds, and it runs inside the synchronous request path of the single shared Node.js process.
intended_behavior: Validating an accepted import cell is linear in its length, or the cell is length-capped (for example at 254 characters, the RFC 5321 limit) and rejected before any regex runs. Validating a 5 MiB file takes milliseconds, not minutes.

trace.description: Any authenticated member with role agent or higher in any organization of the install can upload a file.
The only size bound is file.size > CSV_MAX_BYTES (5 MiB, lib/contacts/csv.ts:148). No per-cell bound exists.
parseCsv or vcfParaLinhas produce the rows in linear time. One data row fits within the 500-row cap.
mapLinha runs synchronously for each row, before the Zod schema at line 179.
email = get('email') is only trimmed. Unlike name and display_name (lines 407-409), it is not sliced.
/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(email) backtracks in O(n^2) on 'a@' + '.'×n + '@' and blocks the event loop for the duration.

evidence.description: CSV_MAX_BYTES = 5 MiB is the only bound on the cell length.
name and display_name are sliced to 200 characters, but email is not.
The rejection reason echoes the whole email cell back into the response body.
The vCard path caps a logical line at 20,000 characters. That bounds each EMAIL value at about 0.3 s, but a 5 MiB file holds about 250 such cards.
CMD ["node","server.js"]: one process and one event loop serve every route for every organization.
The healthcheck is a raw TCP connect. The kernel accepts connections while the event loop is blocked, and restart: unless-stopped does not act on health, so nothing restarts the process.
The shipped reverse proxy forwards to app:3000 with no request_body max_size, so the 5 MiB application cap is the effective limit.

conditions.description: An authenticated session of any member.
Role agent or higher in any organization on the install. The import route requires agent.

The shipped topology runs one app container with one node server.js process, behind the kit's Caddy, which has no body limit. An external proxy in Traefik mode with its own body limit would shrink the stall quadratically but not remove it: a 1 MiB cap still allows about 12 minutes (extrapolated).

payloads: CSV text: 'nome,email\nDummy,a@' + '.'.repeat(k) + '@\n' for k in 2500, 5000, 10000, 20000, 40000

Native-interface equivalent (not executed): POST /api/v1/contacts/import with an agent session cookie and multipart/form-data field file=contatos.csv (text/csv) containing that text. The 5 MiB cap admits k up to about 5,242,860.

title: Agent role can set or clear the manager-only 'personal' and 'always human' contact marks through a direct PostgREST update, with no audit row
description:
Migration 0540 added contacts.is_personal (a personal contact: no AI agent, campaign or prospecting message may go to it) and contacts.ai_opt_out (always human: the AI never answers and no return-to-AI undoes it). The column comments and both routes say only a manager or owner changes them. POST/DELETE /api/v1/contacts/[id]/personal and /always-human require role manager through resolveAuthDual, and each change writes a contacts.personal_* or contacts.always_human_* audit row.

The database does not enforce that floor. The authenticated role has GRANT ALL on contacts. The only role floor on UPDATE is the restrictive policy contacts_update_de_atendente, which requires agent. The session column guard fn_contato_colunas_de_controle already rejects JWT writes to is_blocked, is_anonymized and is_merged_into with 42501, but it was never extended to the 0540 columns. The session audit trigger fires only on consent, source and force_human.

An agent can therefore read their own access token from GET /api/v1/auth/realtime-token and send PATCH /rest/v1/contacts with the public anon key to clear or set either mark, and no audit row is written. The effects stay inside the tenant:
- Clearing ai_opt_out removes the only barrier in devolverAtendimentoAoAgente, so the agent-level reactivate-bot route hands an always-human contact back to the AI.
- Clearing is_personal makes the owner's personal contacts eligible again for the AI agent, campaigns and prospecting.
- Setting is_personal silently drops a customer from the AI agent, campaign preparation and prospecting (the mark does not reach automation rules or the chatbot).

A viewer is still blocked by the restrictive policy, and nothing crosses tenants.

Reproduced on a throwaway Postgres 16 with the Supabase prelude and the full baseline. As an agent JWT, the is_blocked update was rejected with 42501, while both marks updated and left no audit row about them.

title: Invited participant gains owner-level control over another agent's private conversation (2-argument visibility rule ignores is_private)
description: Migration 0544 lets the owner of a conversation, or a manager, invite a colleague to it. Its stated contract is that the invite widens read and reply only. In the code this reads 'Ler não é mandar', 'O convite permite responder, sem mudar o responsável ou encerrar o atendimento', and the dono único 'continua sendo quem FECHA e TRANSFERE'. That contract is enforced in two places, and both use the 2-argument fn_can_view_conversation(org, assigned_to_user_id). The first is the route gate exigirControleDaConversa, used by POST close, POST setor, POST chatbot and PATCH status. The second is the 0544 restrictive UPDATE/DELETE policies on conversations and messages. The 2-argument rule has no privacy term. In visibility_mode 'all' it is true for every agent. In the default 'own_and_unassigned' it is true for every agent when the conversation has no owner. Before the invite, an agent cannot touch another agent's private conversation, because conversations_select and fn_conversation_assign use the privacy-aware 3-argument rule and hide it. After the invite, the participant branch of conversations_select makes the row visible, and the 2-argument control check passes. On the installed baseline, in mode 'all', the invited agent can do the following to the owner's private conversation. (1) Pass the route gate, so it can close the conversation, start a chatbot, or move it to a sector. The sector route's service-role release then unassigns the original owner, who can no longer see the conversation, while the invitee keeps access. (2) Through the Supabase REST API with its own JWT: set is_private=false, which exposes the whole history to every agent who was never invited; assign the conversation to itself, which locks the owner out; set status='closed'; and rewrite or hard-delete the owner's outbound messages. The same holds in the default mode for an unassigned private conversation that a manager shared. Only the RPC path fn_conversation_assign refuses the invitee, because it uses the 3-argument rule.
root_cause: The post-invite control predicate reuses fn_can_view_conversation(uuid, uuid) (baseline.sql 5305), which omits the is_private condition. The privacy-aware rule that governed the agent's authority before the invite is fn_can_view_conversation(uuid, uuid, boolean) (baseline.sql 42909), used by conversations_select (51238) and fn_conversation_assign (43091). The 0544 restrictive policies conversation_participant_read_is_not_control_update/delete (51259, 51264) and message_participant_reply_is_not_history_update/delete (51271, 51286), and lib/inbox/controle-da-conversa.ts:19, call the 2-argument overload. For private conversations the control predicate is therefore wider than the read predicate the invite was meant to extend, and the participant branch supplies the read access that used to block everything else.
intended_behavior: An invited participant may read and reply only. Changing the owner, status, sector, privacy or chatbot state of a private conversation, and editing or deleting another person's messages in it, stays limited to its assigned agent, managers/admins and the platform admin. This is the rule fn_conversation_assign already applies through fn_can_view_conversation(org, assigned_to_user_id, is_private), and the one the 0544 comments and the gate's error message promise.

trace.description: The caller is an agent+ cookie user (requireRole('agent'), line 40). The route reads the conversation with the session client (lines 57-64). Under RLS the private conversation is returned to an invited participant.

Besides the 3-argument privacy rule, the policy has an 'or exists (conversation_participants ... user_id = auth.uid() and left_at is null)' branch that makes another agent's private conversation readable by the invitee.
Calls rpc fn_can_view_conversation with only p_org and p_assigned_to_user_id, which resolves to the 2-argument overload. is_private is never passed.
Returns true for any agent when visibility_mode='all', and for an unassigned conversation in 'own_and_unassigned'. It has no is_private term, so the gate passes for the invitee.
A service-role UPDATE moves the conversation to the sector the caller chose, silences the bot (bot_silenced_until='infinity') and clears active_ai_agent_id.

Service-role fn_conversation_assign(to=null, 'release') runs when the owner is not in the sector. With auth.uid() null, its 3-argument visibility check (baseline.sql 43090-43093) is skipped. The original owner is unassigned and loses sight of the private conversation, while the invitee keeps it.

evidence.description: The comment claims the gate reuses the pre-invite rule that protects fn_conversation_assign, but that function uses the 3-argument, privacy-aware form.
0544 contract: 'Ler não é mandar: o convite (e o setor) não ampliam UPDATE/DELETE da conversa. Quem já escrevia continua escrevendo.'

Restrictive UPDATE policy conversation_participant_read_is_not_control_update uses the 2-argument rule. The verifier probe confirms that pg_get_expr of the installed policy is fn_can_view_conversation(organization_id, assigned_to_user_id).

Restrictive message UPDATE policy uses the 2-argument rule, and so does the DELETE policy at 51286. In mode 'all' the invitee passes both for the owner's outbound messages. Verifier probe V2e: UPDATE body = 1 row, DELETE = 1 row.
The 3-argument overload adds 'not is_private or platform admin or assignee or manager/admin'. Probe V1: it returns false for the invitee, while the 2-argument gate returns true.
fn_conversation_assign authorizes a logged-in caller with the 3-argument rule. Probe V2d: the invitee's RPC claim returns 0 rows. This is the only control path that is correctly bound.

The permissive policy conversations_agent_update allows any agent+ of the org to update any visible row. The table has GRANT ALL to authenticated (line 4585), and fn_conversa_colunas_do_atendimento (43428) does not protect is_private, assigned_to_user_id or status. So the restrictive 0544 policy is the only row-level guard on those columns.
The privacy route itself allows only a manager or the assignee. The direct REST UPDATE of is_private under the 2-argument restrictive policy bypasses this rule.
The close route relies on exigirControleDaConversa, then closes through the service-role fn_service_status at line 191.
Manual chatbot start relies on the same 2-argument gate.
PATCH /conversations/[id] status changes rely on the same gate before the service-role fn_service_status (line 577).
The shipped invariant seeds only visibility_mode 'own' (lines 102 and 104), the one mode where the 2- and 3-argument rules agree, so the disagreement is untested.

title: Host update agent installs whatever git ref the app database names and auto-forces downgrades
description: Since O9 (commit b2c8ed582, a port of upstream #2756/#2757), the heartbeat response from /api/v1/system/agent carries to_version verbatim from the newest dispatched system_update_runs row. agent.sh takes it as ALVO, falls back to its own LATEST_TAG only when it is empty, and appends --force itself whenever ALVO is an ancestor of HEAD. update.sh validates --to only with git rev-parse --verify <ref>^{commit}. With --to present it never consults the published-release authority ultima_release_estavel, and with --force it skips the downgrade guard. It then checks out the ref. It re-sources _common.sh and manutencao.sh from that commit as the host cron user. It re-applies that commit's supabase/baseline.sql to the production database and pins all images to :<ref>; if the pull or up fails, it builds and runs images from the checked-out tree. Accepted targets include any old release tag, tags with no published release, any historical commit SHA, relative refs such as v1.1.0~1, and remote-tracking refs such as origin/main (an unreleased tip newer than the installed release, which is not even forced). Before this diff the agent only ever passed its own LATEST_TAG. The design spec (line 36), the agent route header (lines 6-7) and agent.sh's own header (line 4) all state that even a compromised app chooses only WHEN the signed tag's update.sh runs, never WHAT runs. Now anything that can write a dispatched run row (the service-role key in the app/worker/voice-agent .env) or answer the heartbeat chooses the version the host installs, including forced downgrades that revert code, kit and DB-function security fixes. With only INTERNAL_SECRET (held by the scheduler and the app), an attacker can rewrite system_version.latest_version through a heartbeat or plant a failed run's from_version through a rollback message. The owner's next update, rollback or force click then dispatches the chosen ref. On the route side, ehVersaoPublicada (/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+/) is not end-anchored. Calibration against the comparable baseline: upstream v1.116.0 (tag present in this clone) end-anchors ehVersaoPublicada and makes agent.sh refuse any ALVO not matching ^v?\d+\.\d+\.\d+$, allowing a rollback only to the host-recorded origin (.update-de-onde-vim). Its stated reason is that whoever can write the host-app channel must not be able to reinstall an arbitrary old version with its baseline and functions. The fork's port lacks both guards.
root_cause: hostgator-setup-kit/agent.sh:437-451 trusts the app-supplied to_version as the update target and adds --force itself for any ancestor ref. hostgator-setup-kit/update.sh treats --to as operator-authorized: it consults ultima_release_estavel only when --to is absent (line 107), validates the ref only by git rev-parse (lines 109-110), and runs the downgrade guard only without FORCE (line 176). Neither side binds the target to the host's published release or to a version this host recorded before its last update. The app-side filter lib/system/update-run.ts:283 is not end-anchored, and the update route uses system_version.latest_version (writable by any INTERNAL_SECRET heartbeat) as the plain-update target with no format or ordering check (update/route.ts:237).

title: Media persist worker re-attaches a stored media object and stale metadata to a message the LGPD cascade has just anonymized
description:
persistMessageMedia consumes media.persist_requested, which is emitted when an inbound WhatsApp media message is ingested. It reads the message row (media_url set, media_storage_path null, metadata) and downloads the bytes from the channel. It uploads them to whatsapp-media at {org}/{conversation}/{message}.{ext}. It then writes media_storage_path, media_size_bytes, media_mime and the metadata snapshot it read, with an UPDATE filtered only by id and organization_id.

Suppose fn_lgpd_cascade_redact_contact commits inside that download/upload window. The cascade sets the body to '[mensagem anonimizada]', nulls the media columns and sets metadata to '{}'. Its trigger trg_redigir_conversas_ao_anonimizar does the same for group messages the titular wrote. Both only enqueue media paths that already exist, so the object being uploaded is never queued for deletion. The worker's write then puts the media pointer and the pre-redaction metadata back on the anonymized row. For a group message written by the titular, that metadata is group_sender {name, phone, lid}: the identifiers the cascade uses to find the titular. For a 1:1 WAHA message it is {raw_type, ack_name}.

Nothing reclaims the result:
- The daily orphan sweep skips objects referenced by messages.media_storage_path.
- A second cascade run returns already_anonymized.
- The catch-up sweep only checks leads and activities.

Any org member who can see the conversation can again get a 1-hour signed URL to the media. For non-group messages the worker also emits media.derive_requested. The derive worker then downloads the restored object and passes it to the vision/transcription provider. Only after that does the redaction guard added in this diff skip its own write. The object stays until media retention removes it: media_retention_days after the message's creation (default 365, floor 30), only while media_retention_enforced is on and the org has no open LGPD request. With the switch off it stays indefinitely.
root_cause:
markStatus in workers/media-persist-worker.ts:76-83 writes the metadata snapshot read at :51-61. At :148-152 it also writes the new media_storage_path. The write is filtered only by id and organization_id. It is not a compare-and-set against the state the worker read: neither media_url, which the cascade nulls, nor the MENSAGEM_REDIGIDA body that marks a redacted row.

fn_lgpd_cascade_redact_contact (supabase/baseline.sql:46033, 46229) and fn_redigir_conversas_ao_anonimizar (45885-45895, 45957-45963) only enqueue paths that are already in media_storage_path, so they cannot see an upload still in flight. In this same diff the sibling derive worker received exactly this guard (workers/media-derive-worker.ts:315, commit b4e5bebe7); the persist worker did not. The unguarded markStatus('failed') on the last attempt can likewise restore the stale metadata snapshot, without a pointer.
intended_behavior: Once a contact is anonymized, its messages keep the body '[mensagem anonimizada]', null media pointers and empty metadata. The same applies to group messages that the titular wrote. Every media object of those messages is removed from whatsapp-media (CLAUDE.md LGPD: the redact cascade removes message media from storage). A queued media processor that started before the cascade must not write pointers or metadata back to a redacted row, and any object it uploaded must be deleted or queued for deletion.

trace.description: An inbound WhatsApp media message from the contact is stored with media_url set, and media.persist_requested is emitted for it. Group messages follow the same path: lib/grupos/ingest.ts:318, with metadata.group_sender at :146-149.
The service-role SELECT reads the row: media_url set, media_storage_path null, and metadata. This metadata becomes the snapshot written back later.
Downloads the media through the channel adapter. This step and the upload below are the window in which the cascade can commit.

v_media_paths only collects rows that already have media_storage_path. The trigger fn_redigir_conversas_ao_anonimizar (45885-45895, plus 45957-45963 for group messages) has the same filter, so the in-flight object is never enqueued.
Step 3 sets body to '[mensagem anonimizada]', nulls media_url, media_mime, media_size_bytes and media_storage_path, and sets metadata '{}'. The cascade then commits.
Uploads the bytes to whatsapp-media at storagePathFor(org, conversation, message, mime), with upsert true.

Runs UPDATE messages SET metadata = {...stale snapshot, media_status:'stored'}, media_storage_path, media_size_bytes, media_mime WHERE id AND organization_id. On the anonymized row this restores the media pointer and the pre-redaction metadata.

evidence.description: markStatus writes {...msg.metadata, media_status} from the initial read, filtered only by .eq('id') and .eq('organization_id') (lines 80-81). It has no predicate on media_url, media_storage_path or body.

The sibling write is guarded with .filter('body','isdistinct',MENSAGEM_REDIGIDA), and the comment says that rewriting a redacted row would bring back what the LGPD cascade erased. The guard was added in-range in b4e5bebe7. The persist worker, changed in-range in 456923eea, has no equivalent.
deriveMediaText receives the bytes downloaded at :167 before the guarded write at :315 is evaluated. A restored object therefore reaches the vision/transcription provider.
After the unguarded write, the persist worker emits media.derive_requested for non-group, non-imported messages.

fn_messages_midia_so_pelo_servidor only blocks pointer changes by authenticated/anon. fn_mensagem_colunas_de_envio (43391) also returns early for any other role. Neither trigger stops the service-role write.
A second run of fn_lgpd_cascade_redact_contact returns already_anonymized immediately, so re-running the cascade does not re-redact the message.
The orphan sweep in fn_enfileirar_midia_vencida skips any whatsapp-media object referenced by messages.media_storage_path. The restored object is never reclaimed as an orphan.

Retention reaches the message only when organizations.media_retention_enforced is true (default true, line 47565). It then needs media_retention_days since the message was created (default 365, floor 30) and no lgpd_requests row in received/processing for the org.
The daily catch-up varrerRedacoesIncompletas detects residue only in crm_leads and crm_lead_activities (idsComResiduo, line 310). It never re-checks messages.
Any org member who can read the message under RLS gets a signed URL (TTL 3600 s, line 28) for the restored media_storage_path.

Group messages store metadata.group_sender {name, phone, lid}. This is the PII that the persist write restores on a group message written by the titular. 1:1 WAHA messages store only {raw_type, ack_name} (lib/waha/ingest.ts:898).

conditions.description: fn_lgpd_cascade_redact_contact must commit between the worker's SELECT and its markStatus UPDATE. That window is one provider download plus one storage upload. Later retries re-read the redacted row and skip on 'no media_url'.

The contact being anonymized has an inbound media message, 1:1 or in an enabled group, whose media.persist_requested attempt is in flight (media_url set, media_storage_path still null). Example: media received about a minute before the anonymization runs.
An org admin runs POST /api/v1/lgpd/anonymize, or the lgpd-redact worker processes a formal request. The later readers are org members allowed to see the conversation.

After the overrun, the object lives until media retention removes it: media_retention_days from the message's creation, default 365, only with media_retention_enforced on and no open LGPD request. With the switch off it lives indefinitely. Derivation is requested only for non-group, non-imported messages.

execution.attacker_perspective: No attacker controls the timing; this is a lifecycle race. The lower-trust parties who benefit afterwards are org members who open the anonymized conversation and the AI provider that the derive worker feeds. The affected party is the data subject whose erasure was carried out.

It creates three inbound image messages with media_url set and media_storage_path null. Their metadata copies the real ingest shapes: {raw_type, ack_name} for 1:1, and {raw_type, group_sender{name, phone, lid}} for the group message written by the titular.

agents/verifier-lgpd-midia/artifacts/evidence/race-replay.sql: a DB-layer replay, one autocommit statement per worker PostgREST call, as service_role. Order: worker SELECT snapshot, cascade RPC, storage.objects insert, worker UPDATE, daily sweep, second cascade, agent read under RLS, and a control showing the compare-and-set write.

agents/verifier-lgpd-midia/artifacts/evidence/worker-e2e-harness.txt: a vitest harness that runs the real persistMessageMedia and deriveMessageMedia against the real baseline schema through a service-role pg shim. The channel download is stubbed so that the real fn_lgpd_cascade_redact_contact commits once both workers have done their SELECT. The provider call, LLM credential resolver and logger are stubbed.
instructions: Inside the parent sandbox with --pg (no network; throwaway Postgres 16 with the Supabase prelude and supabase/baseline.sql applied), run: psql -X -d audit -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f evidence/race-replay.sql. It loads evidence/fixture.sql itself.

In a fresh --pg sandbox run, load evidence/fixture.sql. Then run the harness listed in evidence/worker-e2e-harness.txt with dummy non-secret env NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=dummy, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=dummy: vitest run --config harness/vitest.config.mjs.
Compare each message row before the cascade, after the cascade, and after the worker's final UPDATE. Check whether any storage_redaction_queue row targets the uploaded objects after the daily sweep.
execution.observed_result:
Verifier's own reproductions, two of them.

1. DB replay (agents/verifier-lgpd-midia/artifacts/evidence/race-replay.txt):
- The cascade returned already_anonymized=false, media_paths [], and 0 queue rows. Both rows then had body '[mensagem anonimizada]', null media pointers and metadata {}.
- The worker-equivalent service-role UPDATEs, filtered only by id and organization_id, returned UPDATE 1 each.
- Both rows then had media_storage_path '<org>/<conv>/<msg>.jpg' while contacts.is_anonymized was true. The group row again carried group_sender {name:'Titular Dummy', phone:'+5511988887777', lid:'123456789012345'}.
- With the objects aged 2 days, fn_enfileirar_midia_vencida returned {orfas:0, vencidas:0, expurgadas:0}, and 0 queue rows targeted the objects.
- A second cascade returned already_anonymized=true, and both pointers stayed set.
- An org agent under RLS read both pointers and the group_sender.
- Control: the same race with the proposed guard (media_url unchanged, media_storage_path null, body is distinct from the marker) gave UPDATE 0, and the row stayed redacted.

2. End-to-end harness (agents/verifier-lgpd-midia/artifacts/evidence/worker-e2e.log and worker-e2e-run.txt, 1 test passed):
- The real persistMessageMedia ran for both messages concurrently. The cascade committed during the download and redacted 1 message plus the group message via the trigger, with media_paths [].
- Both uploads landed. Both markStatus UPDATEs ran with filters [eq(id), eq(organization_id)] and returned rows=1, and both workers returned status ok. emit_event(media.derive_requested) ran for the 1:1 message only.
- Final rows: body '[mensagem anonimizada]', media_url null, media_storage_path set. Metadata was {ack_name, raw_type, media_status:'stored'} for the 1:1 message and {raw_type, group_sender{...}, media_status:'stored'} for the group message.
- The real deriveMessageMedia then downloaded the restored object and called deriveMediaText (the provider call, stubbed) with 3 bytes. Its guarded UPDATE returned rows=0, giving status skipped/message_redacted.
- The daily sweep returned orfas 0, and 0 queue rows targeted the restored objects.

remediation.strategy:
Make the persist write a compare-and-set on the state the worker read, as the derive worker already does. Only write when media_url still equals the value read, which the cascade nulls, and the body is not MENSAGEM_REDIGIDA. Use .select('id') to learn whether the row was written. If no row matched, remove the object just uploaded (best effort; once unreferenced, the daily orphan sweep reclaims it if the remove fails) and return skipped. Apply the same guard to markStatus('failed'), so a stale metadata snapshot is never written back to a redacted row.

Do not guard on media_storage_path IS NULL together with a delete-on-miss. Two attempts at the same message share one deterministic path, and the losing attempt would then delete the winner's object.

As defense in depth, have the derive worker read body and skip before downloading when it is the redaction marker, so the bytes never reach the provider. Regression test: the race harness above must end with the rows still redacted, no media_storage_path, a storage remove of the uploaded path, and no deriveMediaText call.

likelihood.reason: The anonymization must commit inside one in-flight persist attempt, which spans a single download and upload. Later retries re-read the redacted row and skip. No attacker can trigger or time it. It happens on its own only when a contact's media arrives shortly before an erasure is executed.

impact.reason: It breaks the LGPD erasure guarantee for the data subject's media bytes. For group messages it also breaks it for the sender identifiers (name, phone, lid). The object is never enqueued for deletion. Org staff can open it through signed URLs until retention or indefinitely, and for 1:1 messages it is sent to the AI provider after the erasure. The exposure stays within the same org and its configured provider. It is not cross-tenant.

confidence.reason: Reproduced independently in two ways on the baseline schema actually installed: a statement-level replay, and the real persist and derive worker code running against the real database and the real cascade function. The baseline accepts the service-role write; no trigger blocks it, no sweep repairs it, and a re-run does not undo it. The only open factor is how often the timing occurs in production.

title: Automation actions, the chatbot, the campaign send-time check and token/MCP senders ignore the 'personal' and 'always human' contact marks
description: Migration 0540 adds two manager-only contact marks. contacts.is_personal promises that nothing automatic goes out to the contact; the UI copy says the AI does not answer, prospecting does not approach and campaigns do not send. contacts.ai_opt_out promises that the AI never answers the contact and that no hand-back undoes the mark. Only some senders read the marks: the agent turn (readStopFlags and the eligibility gate), the CRM handoff notice, prospecting and campaign preparation. The other automatic senders never read them. The automation guard checarGuardasDeContato, shared by send_whatsapp_message, send_ai_message and start_chatbot_flow, checks only is_blocked, phone and marketing declined_at. The visual chatbot's conversation-state queries run before the drain's eligibility gate and read only is_blocked and assignee_kind. The campaign round's per-send revalidation omits is_personal. Finally, the shared outbound sink sendMessageHandler vetoes only is_blocked; the upstream 403 for personal contacts, which the ported prospecting guard still cites, was never ported. The installed database has no function, policy or messages trigger that reads either mark. The same sink-level gap also lets the MCP tool crm_send_whatsapp_message (lib/mcp/tools/messages.ts:89), crm start-conversation, and POST /api/v1/messages with a dsk_ bearer token (actor ai_agent or api_token) send to marked contacts with no mark check. title: An agent-chosen outbound media_url makes GET /api/v1/messages/[id]/media call any WAHA API path with the installation key and return the response
description:
Any organization member with the agent role can create an outbound message whose media_url they choose. They can use POST /api/v1/messages (session cookie, or a dsk_ token with mcp:write), the MCP send tools, or a direct PostgREST insert into public.messages. The send-side anti-SSRF guard (assertUrlDeMidiaSegura) checks only the scheme, host text and resolved IP, never the path or query. It is skipped entirely when media_storage_path is also supplied, and a direct PostgREST insert never runs it. Any public host passes, because a later consumer keeps only the path.

The sender, or anyone else in the organization, can then open GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/media. When the row has no storage object (or signing fails), the route hands any non-null media_url to the WAHA adapter. It never checks the message direction. fetchWahaMedia drops scheme, host and port, keeps the path and query, resolves them against WAHA_API_BASE_URL, and adds the installation-wide X-Api-Key. The route then returns the upstream body and Content-Type with status 200. In effect, the message author picks an authenticated GET against the WAHA admin API and reads the answer.

One WAHA container and one key serve every organization's WhatsApp session, and each organization's session is named org_<8>_<32>. An agent of organization A can therefore first read /api/sessions?all=true, which lists every session's name, status, config and connected account (`me`). They can then read per-session resources of organization B. One example is /api/{session}/groups, which the app itself reads with the same key and which does not depend on the history store. Another is /api/{session}/chats and /api/{session}/chats/{chatId}/messages. Those return data only when that connection has the NOWEB history store enabled, which is off by default and opt-in per connection. Inside a single organization, the same mechanism exposes WAHA-side data, such as groups not enabled in the CRM and stored chats, that is not limited by the agent's RLS scope.
root_cause: Two components disagree about what messages.media_url is. The send path stores it as an arbitrary external URL. It validates only scheme, host and resolved IP, skips that check when media_storage_path is present, and a direct PostgREST INSERT bypasses the API entirely, because the 0499 media-pointer trigger is BEFORE UPDATE only. The media read route treats every media_url, whatever the message direction, as a file reference that the provider advertised. Through the WAHA adapter, fetchWahaMedia then trusts its path and query and replays them with the installation-wide WAHA API key. The comment claiming SSRF is 'impossible by construction' covers only the host rewrite. Nothing limits the path to WAHA's file store or to the message's own session.
intended_behavior: The media route should proxy only media that the provider advertised on an inbound message. The path should be limited to WAHA's file store (/api/files/...) for that message's own session, with no caller-controlled query. No message author should be able to choose the path or query of a server-side request made with the WAHA installation key.

trace.description: resolveAuthDual accepts a session cookie or a dsk_ bearer token (mcp:write) with role agent or higher. sendMessageSchema allows media_url as any z.string().url() and media_storage_path as any 1–500 character string (lib/schemas/messaging.ts:77-78).

assertUrlDeMidiaSegura runs only when media_url is present WITHOUT media_storage_path. The storage path check at lines 563-565 tests the {org}/{conv}/ prefix and literal characters only, not whether the object exists. A fake owned-looking path therefore skips the guard.
When the guard runs, it checks scheme, host text (assertSafeOutboundUrl) and resolved IP (line 43). The path and query are unconstrained, so https://<any public host>/api/<any WAHA path> passes.
media_url (and media_storage_path at line 757) are inserted unchanged into the outbound row through the caller's client before any send happens. The row is kept whether the send succeeds or fails.

The row is read through the caller's RLS client (select at line 57 does not load direction). When there is no storage path, or createSignedUrl fails (lines 89-102), any non-null media_url is passed to adapter.fetchInboundMedia with the message's own WAHA session (line 134).
Passes the raw media_url to fetchWahaMedia. sessionRef is not used to limit the path.
Builds new URL(advertised.pathname + advertised.search, WAHA_API_BASE_URL) and fetches it with X-Api-Key = WAHA_API_KEY (lines 34-38). The upstream Content-Type is kept (line 47).
Returns the upstream WAHA response body and Content-Type with status 200 to the authenticated caller.

evidence.description: Only scheme, host and port are dropped. Any path and query of the stored URL are replayed against the WAHA API base.
The installation-wide WAHA API key is attached to that request.
The route's select does not load direction, so outbound rows are treated like provider-advertised inbound media.
The provider fallback runs for any non-null media_url when no signed storage URL is produced.
The anti-SSRF guard is skipped when media_storage_path is also supplied. media_url is still stored at line 755.
The guard judges only scheme, host text and (line 43) resolved IP. It never looks at the path a later consumer will request.
The 0499 media-pointer trigger is BEFORE UPDATE OF media_url, media_storage_path only. No INSERT control on media_url exists, so an agent can also insert such a row directly through PostgREST.

The restrictive INSERT policy lets agents insert only direction='outbound' rows. Inbound rows come only from service-role ingestion, so a direction check on the read route excludes every agent-written media_url.
A single WAHA_API_BASE_URL/WAHA_API_KEY pair serves the whole installation.
Each organization gets its own session name (org_<8>_<32>) inside that single WAHA.
The app's own WAHA session schema shows that session objects carry `me` (connected account) and config next to name and status. That is what /api/sessions returns for every session.
The app reads /api/{session}/groups with the same key. This was measured on real WAHA and returns the number's groups.
The app reads /api/{session}/chats/{chatId}/messages (and /api/{session}/chats at line 610) with the same key. These return history only when the connection enabled the NOWEB store.
The NOWEB store is disabled by default and is enabled per connection, which bounds what the chats/messages paths can return.
The existing test treats the host rewrite as the anti-SSRF control and asserts that path and query are preserved. There is no assertion that limits the path.
