Chats and messages from /api/{session}/chats... exist only for connections that enabled history storage, which is off by default. Session listing and groups do not depend on it.
What WAHA returns for each chosen GET path. The paths cited are ones the app's own WAHA client calls with the same key; the response contents were not observed against a real WAHA.

In bin/sb (no network, read-only target, env -i allowlist, NODE_ENV=test), one vitest harness chained both halves on the SAME row. The real sendMessageHandler ran with the repository's shared handler double as the RLS client and an agent session actor ({type:'user'}). Database check (evidence/messages-insert-as-agent.sql → .log). In bin/sb --pg with the installed baseline, an agent of a dummy org was set as role authenticated with jwt claims. The agent inserted an outbound messages row with an arbitrary media_url and read it back with the same select the media route uses. As a control, the agent then tried the 0499-guarded UPDATE of media_url.
execution.observed_result: From my own reproduction (not the hunter's artifacts). Send side: A returned 422 unsafe_media_url with 0 inserts. B and C each inserted 1 row with direction=outbound and media_url stored unchanged (send status sent). D skipped the guard and inserted media_url=https://169.254.169.254/api/sessions?all=true; the final status was failed/storage_sign_failed and the row was kept. Read side, on those exact rows: for B the route made exactly one request, to http://waha:3000/api/sessions?all=true with headers {"X-Api-Key":"dummy-installation-wide-waha-key"}, and returned 200 application/json with the upstream body. For C the request went to http://waha:3000/api/org_99999999_fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210/chats?limit=5 with the key, and returned 200. For D, signing failed, the route fell through to the same request to /api/sessions?all=true with the key, and returned 200. All 4 tests passed, exit 0. Database: authenticated has INSERT on public.messages, and fn_message_service_lock does not mention media_url. The agent's direct INSERT of an outbound row with an arbitrary media_url succeeded, and the agent read it back with direction=outbound and an empty media_storage_path. The only media_url trigger is BEFORE UPDATE: the agent's UPDATE of media_url raised media_pointer_server_only, but INSERT is not covered. What a real WAHA returns on each path was not observed.

remediation.strategy:
Fix the read side, because a direct PostgREST insert bypasses any API-side guard. The primary control belongs in fetchWahaMedia: accept only WAHA file-store paths (/api/files/<file> or /api/files/<own sessionRef>/<file>) with no query, and pass the message's sessionRef down from the adapter. Never replay the path or query of an arbitrary stored URL. This alone removes the reach into the WAHA admin API and into other sessions for every row, whoever wrote it.

As defense in depth, the route can also proxy only direction='inbound' rows. Direction is the one discriminator the database enforces on INSERT: the restrictive RLS policy lets agents insert only outbound rows, while sent_via and external_id stay writable. This has a trade-off. Media the operator sends from the phone (lib/waha/ingest.ts:1203-1211) and imported history are also stored as outbound rows with a provider media_url, so with the direction gate their media appears only after the persist worker stores it, normally within the next drain minute. If that window matters, keep proxying outbound rows, but only through the restricted file-store path.

On the send side, also run assertUrlDeMidiaSegura whenever media_url is present, even with media_storage_path. Serve proxied bytes with nosniff and a sandbox CSP.

Update tests/unit/media-waha-source.test.ts, whose current case asserts that the query is preserved. Add these regression tests: an outbound row with media_url https://93.184.215.14/api/sessions makes GET /media return 404 with no fetch; fetchWahaMedia rejects /api/sessions, /api/<other session>/chats, /api/files/<other session>/x.jpg and any query; and a send with media_url plus media_storage_path still runs the URL guard.

likelihood.reason: Requires an authenticated agent-role account in an organization with a WAHA channel. After that it takes two ordinary requests, with no race condition and no victim interaction. Any public hostname passes the send guard, and a direct PostgREST insert skips it entirely.

impact.reason: A low-privileged tenant member gets authenticated read access to the WAHA admin API with the installation-wide key, and the response is relayed to them. On multi-organization installations this exposes every organization's session list, including connected account identity, and each session's groups. Where a connection enabled history storage, it also exposes that organization's chats and messages. Inside one organization, it exposes WAHA-side data that the agent's RLS scope does not cover. The exact data depends on WAHA's responses, which were not observed.

confidence.reason: My own reproduction chained the real send handler and the real media route, adapter and fetcher on the same inserted row. The server made a request with the WAHA key to the path the author chose and relayed the body with status 200. The database check shows that no INSERT-side control exists and that the agent can read the row back. The only unobserved part is what a real WAHA returns per path, and those paths are ones the app's own client reads with the same key.

title: Prospecting XLSX import has no cap on total decompressed size: each ~41 KB of upload adds ~40 MiB of memory in the shared app process
description: POST /api/v1/prospecting/importar passes the uploaded .xlsx to parseXlsx in lib/planilha/ler-arquivo.ts. Its fflate unzipSync filter accepts every entry named xl/worksheets/*.xml, plus workbook, rels and sharedStrings, and only rejects an entry whose declared size is above 40 MiB. fflate 0.8.3 allocates an output buffer of the declared size for each accepted entry (new u8(su) in unzipSync) and returns all of them in one object, so they stay in memory together, although the parser reads only the first sheet. A 40 MiB worksheet of repeated bytes deflates to about 41 KB, so the 2 MB upload cap admits about 51 such entries, roughly 2 GiB. The sibling reader lib/crm-b2b/spreadsheet.ts was fixed for this exact attack on 2026-11-04 (commit eb8f0d145: two-pass inflate and a 48 MiB sum cap); the neutral reader the prospecting import uses was added on 2026-11-17 (39d049d50) from the unfixed version. The single app container in docker-compose.prod.yml serves every organization and has mem_limit 768m (its comment cites a measured peak of 335 MiB).
root_cause: lib/planilha/ler-arquivo.ts:140-149 bounds decompression per entry only (line 147: f.originalSize > XLSX_MAX_XML_BYTES). It inflates every worksheet entry in one unzipSync call (filter at line 146) and keeps the whole result until the parse ends. It neither sums the declared sizes nor limits inflation to the entries the parser reads.
intended_behavior: The comment at ler-arquivo.ts:34-38 states the intent: a small upload must not become hundreds of megabytes of server memory. Total inflated bytes per parse should be capped, and only workbook.xml, its rels, the resolved first sheet and sharedStrings should be inflated, as lib/crm-b2b/spreadsheet.ts:31-39 and 140-187 already do.

trace.description: Session-only multipart upload. disparo_em_massa module gate at line 40 (404 when off), role admin at line 45, bearer tokens get 403 at line 53, body capped at 2 MB + 64 KB at line 58, file capped at 2 MB at line 85.
parseImportFile(await file.arrayBuffer(), file.name, { maxLinhas: PLANILHA_MAX_LINHAS }) runs before any write, in preview mode as well.
Any filename ending in .xlsx goes to parseXlsx.
unzipSync inflates every accepted xl/worksheets/*.xml entry into a buffer of its declared size and returns all of them at once.

evidence.description: The only size check is per entry (originalSize > 40 MiB). There is no running sum.
The filter accepts any number of xl/worksheets/*.xml entries, although only one sheet is read (line 171).
The sibling defines XLSX_MAX_TOTAL_XML_BYTES = 48 MiB. Its comment at lines 31-38 describes this attack: about 50 entries, about 2 GB, a 768 MB container shared by every organization.
The sibling enforces the summed declared size and inflates only the entries it reads (lines 166 and 183).
mem_limit 768m on the app service. The comment at line 15 gives a measured peak of 335 MiB, and restart: unless-stopped (line 37) restarts it after an OOM kill.

conditions.description: The attacker holds the admin role in an organization and uses a browser session (bearer tokens are refused).
The installation-level module disparo_em_massa is enabled. It is off by default, and with it off the route returns 404.

title: Prospecting XLSX reader pads each row up to an attacker-chosen column index and keeps every padded row until the sheet ends, so a kilobyte-sized upload allocates hundreds of MiB
description: lib/planilha/ler-arquivo.ts was added in the audited diff (commit 39d049d50). Its parseXlsx takes each cell's column index from the letters of its r= reference through indiceDaColuna, with no upper bound on the letters or the index. Before storing the cell value it runs while (celulas.length < i) celulas.push(""), so every row becomes a dense array as long as its highest referenced column, whatever the header width. Every non-empty row array is then retained in matriz until the whole sheet has been parsed: the 500-row limit (line 75) and the trim to header width (line 80) run only afterwards. Two shapes follow. One reference beyond Excel's columns: a single <c r="ZZZZZ2"> cell makes that row 12,356,630 entries long; in a 920-byte upload this produced 274-329 MiB of peak RSS growth and 436-567 ms of synchronous parsing in two independent runs, and the parse still returned ok. Excel-legal references across many rows: 2,000 data rows that each reference column XFD (index 16,383), zipped to 1,419 bytes, grew peak RSS by about 403 MiB before the row-limit error was returned, and growth is linear in the number of rows, which is bounded only by the 40 MiB decompressed-XML cap. Capping the column at XFD alone therefore does not bound the parse. The in-scope caller is POST /api/v1/prospecting/importar, preview included, which runs the parse in the shared Next.js app process. That process is the app container with mem_limit 768m and a documented 335 MiB measured peak. The decompressed-size cap (XLSX_MAX_XML_BYTES) and the 2 MB upload cap do not bound this, because the input is tiny. Out-of-scope note: lib/crm-b2b/spreadsheet.ts:198-200 has the same pattern and serves POST /api/v1/imports, but that file was not changed in the audited diff, so it is pre-existing and not part of this record.
root_cause: lib/planilha/ler-arquivo.ts:188-193. The cell-reference regex accepts any number of letters (/\br="([A-Z]+\d*)"/i), indiceDaColuna (lines 116-119) turns them into an unbounded index, and that index is the padding target of a dense row array (line 190) that is bounded neither by Excel's last column (XFD, index 16,383) nor by the header width. Every padded row is retained in matriz (line 193), and the row limit (line 75) and the header-width trim (line 80) apply only after the whole sheet has been parsed. Memory therefore grows with the referenced column index times the number of rows, and the number of rows is limited only by the 40 MiB decompressed-XML cap.
intended_behavior: Work and memory for parsing an uploaded sheet should be bounded by the upload and the import limits. No row should be materialised wider than the header (or a small fixed column cap while the header is read), parsing should stop as soon as the row limit is exceeded, and a cell reference beyond Excel's column limit should be rejected, never used to allocate a row array of that length or shifted into another column.

remediation.strategy: Bound the parse by the import limits, not only by Excel's. (1) Never materialise a row wider than needed: while the header row is read, ignore cells at or beyond a small fixed cap (for example 256 columns; the prospecting sheet uses a handful of named columns), and after it, ignore cells beyond the header width instead of padding to them; matrizParaPlanilha trims those columns anyway, so the output is unchanged, except that a data row whose only non-empty cells lie beyond the header is no longer returned as an all-blank row (and no longer counts toward the row limit). (2) Apply the row limit inside the loop: stop and return the row-limit error as soon as matriz holds more than maxLinhas + 1 non-empty rows. (3) Reject references with more than three letters or an index at or above 16,384 (XFD) rather than shifting the value into the next column. Alternatively, store cells sparsely as index/value pairs and build header-width rows in matrizParaPlanilha, but the in-loop row limit is still needed. Apply the same change to the sibling lib/crm-b2b/spreadsheet.ts (pre-existing, outside this diff). Regression tests: a workbook with a cell r="ZZZZZ2" is rejected, and a workbook with 2,000 rows each referencing XFD is rejected, both in a few milliseconds with bounded memory; ordinary 500-row and 501-row sheets keep their current results.

title: Prospecting XLSX reader parses unterminated XML tags in quadratic time: a 1.3 KB upload blocks the shared app event loop for 12.7 s, and the stall grows quadratically
description: After decompression, parseXlsx extracts shared strings, rows, cells and text runs with lazy regexes of the form open-tag, lazy any-char, close-tag. When an opening tag has no matching close, V8's backtracking engine scans to the end of the string, fails, and retries at the next opening tag, so the cost is O(n^2) in the XML size. Neither the 40 MiB per-entry cap nor the 2 MB upload cap bounds this: a repeated '<si>' compresses to a few hundred bytes per 100 KB, and 40 MiB holds about 10.5 million such tags. parseImportFile runs synchronously, with no await inside parseXlsx, in the route handler of the single Next.js process, which serves the UI, API, WhatsApp webhooks and cron calls of every organization. The compose healthcheck is a raw TCP connect (docker-compose.prod.yml:50) that the kernel completes while the event loop is blocked, and Docker does not restart a merely unhealthy container, so nothing ends the stall early. The same regex class was already rewritten as forward scans for prospect HTML (lib/prospecting/leitura-do-html.ts:5-11) but not here; the sibling lib/crm-b2b/spreadsheet.ts shares the pattern.
root_cause: lib/planilha/ler-arquivo.ts:174 (sharedStrings <si>), 180 (<row>), 186 (<c>) and 111 (<t>) call matchAll with a lazy any-char scan to a closing tag, and line 125 (<v>) uses the same shape with exec. Every unterminated opening tag costs a scan to the end of the string. No size or time limit applies at this stage beyond the 40 MiB per-entry inflate cap.
intended_behavior: Parsing a spreadsheet the server already accepted should cost time linear in its size, as in the forward-scanning rewrite in leitura-do-html.ts. Malformed XML should end the scan as soon as no further closing tag exists.

trace.description: Session-only multipart upload of a .xlsx of at most 2 MB. Requires the admin role (line 45) and the disparo_em_massa module (line 40).
parseImportFile runs on the request's event loop; its body is synchronous, so the await does not yield during the parse.
xl/sharedStrings.xml and the sheet XML (each up to 40 MiB declared) are inflated from a few hundred bytes.

The lazy shared-string regex matchAll over unterminated <si> tags costs quadratic time. The row regex at line 180 (measured), and the cell, text and value regexes at lines 186, 111 and 125, have the same shape.

evidence.description: matchAll(/<si>([\s\S]*?)<\/si>/g) runs over the whole sharedStrings text.
The row regex /<row\b([^>]*?)(?:\/>|>([\s\S]*?)<\/row>)/g has the same lazy any-char-to-close-tag shape over the sheet XML.
The repository documents and fixes this exact class for HTML ('abertura sem fechamento ... segundos, ou minutos, para 200 KB') but not for XLSX.
The healthcheck is a raw TCP connect from a separate node process, which succeeds while the server's event loop is blocked.
The sibling reader (manager role via app/api/v1/imports/route.ts:63) has the same <si>, <row> and <c> regexes at lines 190, 194 and 196.

conditions.description: Admin role in an organization, using a browser session.
The disparo_em_massa module is enabled on the installation. It is off by default.

Variant: sheet1.xml ending in '<row>' x k with no closing </row> (k=32000 is a 950-byte file).
instructions: In the network-less sandbox, build each workbook in memory with fflate from the target's node_modules (verifier harness h/measure-regex.mts).

In a fresh tsx process per size, time one call of the target's parseImportFile(bytes, 'lista.xlsx', {maxLinhas: 2000}) for k = 4000, 8000, 16000, 32000, 64000 and 128000 (<si>), and k = 8000, 16000, 32000 (<row>).
Repeat k=16000 and 32000 (<si>) through lib/crm-b2b/spreadsheet.ts to confirm the sibling shares the pattern.
execution.observed_result: Verifier's own bounded reproduction (agents/verifier-planilha/artifacts/evidence/xlsx-unterminated-tag-timing.log). ler-arquivo.ts with <si>: k=4000 17 ms; 8000 53 ms; 16000 263 ms; 32000 760 ms; 64000 2,707 ms (1,080-byte upload); 128000 12,721 ms (1,328-byte upload). Larger sizes were not run. If no closing tag exists after some position, none exists after any later position, so from then on only self-closing tags can match and the tail is never re-read. A forward scan that runs indexOf for the closing tag again after every unterminated opening tag is still quadratic: measured at 4,145 ms for 32,000 unterminated <si> (slower than the current regex) and 64,016 ms for 128,000. The helper below took 50 ms for 1,000,000 and returned the same results as the current regexes on well-formed XLSX XML (agents/final-arquivos/artifacts/evidence/xlsx-fix-helper-timing.log). For opening tags only (<sheet at line 164 and <Relationship at line 167), use a second helper that stops at the first opening tag with no '>'. Those two lines have the same class of cost. A <sheet or <Relationship with no '>', repeated 32,000 times, took 3,223 ms (workbook.xml) and 6,308 ms (rels) from uploads under 1.5 KB (agents/final-arquivos/artifacts/evidence/xlsx-workbook-rels-regex-timing.log), so a fix that covers only lines 111, 125, 174, 180 and 186 leaves the parse quadratic. Optionally, also cap the sharedStrings and sheet XML that are read well below 40 MiB. Add a regression test that times unterminated <si>, <row>, <c>, <t> and <v> inputs, and <sheet and <Relationship inputs with no '>', at about 1M tags each, and expects each to finish well under one second.

impact.reason: A request of about 1 KB blocked the event loop for 12.7 s (measured), and the duration grows quadratically at the attacker's choice. During the stall the single shared process serves no UI, API, webhook or cron request for any organization, and neither the TCP healthcheck nor the restart policy ends it. Stalls of minutes to hours are extrapolated, not run. No data is exposed.

confidence.reason: Superlinear growth was measured directly on the real target function with tiny inputs in an independent reproduction, for two of the regexes. The same pattern is documented and already fixed elsewhere in the repository.

title: Prospect site audit can be bypassed with DNS rebinding: the guard and fetch resolve the name separately, and the internal response is stored, shown to the tenant admin and fed to the outreach AI
description: buscar() approves each hop by resolving the hostname twice: criarVerificadorPadrao at site-fetch.ts:144, then assertDestinoResolvidoSeguro at outbound-ip.ts:104. It then calls the global fetch with the hostname URL; fetch resolves the name a third time, and nothing pins the connection to the vetted addresses. The URL is any http/https URL with any port. It comes from a tenant admin's own import spreadsheet (lib/prospecting/planilha.ts:194, safePublicLink checks only the protocol) or from third-party Google Maps listings (the website field from the Apify or Scavio providers, schema.ts:484). The verificar_sites and reanalisar_site actions and the automatic preparation tick all audit it. The fetch is not blind: up to 1200 chars of the response's title, headings and visible text are stored as data.site.conteudo_resumo, returned to the org admin by GET /api/v1/prospecting, and injected as 'Detalhe' into the AI prompt that writes the WhatsApp message to the listing's phone. The residual-risk note in outbound-ip.ts:11-13 and 88-91 rests on three assumptions: a manager+ insider author, a blind webhook, and pinning breaking TLS. None of them holds for this path, and lib/extensions/download.ts already pins the vetted addresses while keeping SNI. Code-level reproduction (verifier, sandbox): the guard saw a public address, fetch connected to 127.0.0.1, and the loopback page's text came back in conteudo_resumo. Real-world exploitability and impact depend on deployment facts listed as blockers.
claimed_root_cause: lib/prospecting/site-fetch.ts:229-235 checks hostLiberado(atual), which performs fresh DNS lookups (line 144 and outbound-ip.ts:104), and then calls fetchFn(atual, ...) with the unpinned hostname. The global fetch resolves again, a time-of-check to time-of-use gap, so an attacker-run authoritative DNS with TTL 0 can answer a public address to the guard and a private one to the connection.

trace.description: An org admin (session) imports a spreadsheet; its website column becomes data.website through siteDaCelula (lib/prospecting/planilha.ts:194), which accepts any http/https URL and port. The alternative source is provider listings (lib/prospecting/schema.ts:484).
The admin's 'Verificar agora' runs enriquecerSitesPendentes for the campaign; reanalisar_site (line 328) calls auditarSite directly, and the tick does the same through lib/prospecting/preparo.ts:249.
auditarSites(rows.map(r => r.website), ..., fetch, undefined, ...) uses the global fetch and the default verifier.
busca = await buscar(url, fetchFn, verificar)
hostLiberado: recusarSSRF, then two DNS lookups (line 144 and outbound-ip.ts:104) judge the address the name resolves to now.
fetchFn(atual) with the hostname URL performs a third, unpinned resolution and connects to whatever it returns.
conteudo_resumo = montarResumo(html) of the response, in a non-provisional verdict.
The verdict, including conteudo_resumo, is merged into prospecting_candidates.data.site.
p.data, including site.conteudo_resumo, is returned to the org admin, and becomes 'Detalhe' in the AI outreach data (lib/prospecting/estrategia-site.ts:649).

evidence.description: The code declares the DNS-rebinding window between check and connect as a known residual risk, 'fora do modelo de ameaca desta fase'.
The residual-risk reasoning assumes the URL author is a manager+ insider configuring a blind webhook; here the authors are a tenant admin or third-party listings, and the response is read back.
It claims that pinning the IP 'muda o SNI/Host e quebra TLS'.
pinnedLookup in the same repository connects only to the vetted addresses (passed as lookup at line 226) and keeps SNI (servername at line 228), so pinning is feasible.
The spreadsheet website cell is accepted as any http/https URL (safePublicLink checks the protocol only).
The fetched text summary is added to the AI prompt data as 'Detalhe'.

blockers: Whether the deployed resolver chain honors TTL 0, so that the guard's two lookups and fetch's lookup milliseconds later can get different answers, is a deployment fact not visible in the repository. The chain is musl getaddrinfo in the node:22-alpine image, then Docker's embedded DNS on the compose network, then the VPS upstream resolver.

Which internal HTTP endpoints return useful content to a plain GET carrying the attacker's Host header from the app container decides the real data exposure. Candidates are cloud metadata (IMDSv1, DigitalOcean), host services on the Docker gateway, and compose services without authentication; WAHA and srh require keys, and a 401 is classified as nao-medido with no summary. This depends on the VPS provider and stack.

Whether any installation that hosts several organizations has the off-by-default disparo_em_massa module enabled. Without it every prospecting route returns 404 and the path is unreachable; on a single-organization installation the tenant admin is usually also the operator.

validation_plan.local: Verifier's own reproduction in the network-less sandbox (agents/verifier-planilha/artifacts/evidence/site-fetch-rebinding.log; harness h/rebind.mts). Only dns.lookup and dns.promises.lookup were patched, before import, for two dummy names; everything else was the real auditarSite with its default verifier and Node 22 global fetch, against a dummy HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 inside the sandbox's own network namespace. rebind.test: lookups 1-2 (the guard) got 93.184.216.34, lookup 3 (fetch) got 127.0.0.1, and the server received 'GET / Host=rebind.test:<port>'. The verdict was a definitive site-ruim, HTTP 200, with conteudo_resumo holding the loopback page's title, h1 and text. Control internal.test (always 127.0.0.1): the guard blocked it (fora-do-ar) and the server received nothing. After a fix that resolves once, checks every address and connects through a pinned lookup (like lib/extensions/download.ts pinnedLookup, with servername for TLS), rerun the harness: no third lookup may happen, the loopback server must receive nothing, and the verdict must be fora-do-ar or nao-medido.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner, on a staging copy of the VPS stack with throwaway data (not production prospects): inside the app container, run node to call dns.promises.lookup three times in quick succession against a test name on an operator-controlled authoritative DNS with TTL 0 that answers a public test IP twice, then a private test IP, and confirm whether the third call sees the private answer or whether Docker's embedded DNS or the upstream resolver pins the first. Then, from inside the app container, list which internal addresses answer an unauthenticated GET with a foreign Host header (169.254.169.254, the Docker gateway on common ports, the compose service names and ports) to size what a rebinding fetch could read. Finally, record whether the disparo_em_massa module is enabled on any multi-organization installation.

title: Reply address accepts any @lid from the last inbound message, so a phone removed from the contact keeps receiving its replies while the screen announces the principal
description: chatSegueNaFicha returns true for every '@lid' chat without comparing it to the lids still bound to the contact. That means contacts.wa_lid and contact_phones.wa_lid are never consulted. chatIdDaUltimaRecebida, which serves sendMessageHandler, the AI runtime, typing presence and edit/revoke, and its SQL copy in the watchdog redrive therefore keep addressing the conversation to the last inbound @lid after that lid has been unbound from the contact. When an operator removes an extra phone, its contact_phones row and wa_lid are deleted, and the next message from that WhatsApp account creates a separate contact. Yet while the contact keeps at least one other extra, all outbound of the original conversation still go to the removed account's @lid. That covers AI replies, follow-ups, scheduled and human messages. The reply-address endpoint binds @lid to the principal's or an extra's wa_lid and so tells the operator replies go to the principal, the opposite of what the send path does. The helper's own doc comment says a number that left the contact returns null, and the @c.us path does honor this. The same gap also defeats removing a bogus extra added through contact-phones:extra-sem-escopo-da-conversa, when that attacker wrote through an @lid chat.
root_cause: lib/waha/ultima-recebida.ts:39 returns true for any chat ending in '@lid'. The @c.us/@s.whatsapp.net case is checked against the contact's numbers (mesmoTelefoneNaLista), and reply-address binds the lid (route.ts:123-130). The send-path helper never reads wa_lid, so two consumers of the same value disagree. The same unbound rule is copied into lib/agent-engine/edge/crm/session-reconciler.ts:230.
intended_behavior: A last-inbound @lid should be used as the reply address only while it equals the principal's wa_lid or an extra's wa_lid. Otherwise the helper should return null so the regular rule (the contact's own wa_lid or phone) applies. That is what reply-address already announces, and what the helper's comment promises.

The contact still has another extra, so the last-inbound rule applies.

The stale @lid takes precedence over the contact's own wa_lid.

The doc comment states that a number which left the contact also returns null. For @lid it does not. The @c.us control in the verifier run did return null.

The watchdog redrive copies the same unbound rule into its own code path. Observed: it POSTed W's queued AI reply to 999999999999999@lid.

conditions.description: An operator with role agent removes an extra phone in an ordinary workflow, with no malice needed. The receiving party is whoever holds the WhatsApp account behind the removed number.
The contact keeps at least one other extra phone, and the conversation's last inbound message came through the removed number's @lid chat (WAHA NOWEB @lid addressing).
The outbound happens before the customer writes again from a number or lid still bound to the contact.
The conversation's channel is WAHA (respondePelaUltimaRecebida).

execution.attacker_perspective: The holder of a WhatsApp account (lid 999999999999999, +5531992220000) whose number an operator has just removed from customer W's record. This party passively receives W's conversation traffic.

Its C2 block creates W and V with two extras each and ingests one inbound through the first extra (@lid for W, @c.us for V). It then deletes that extra as AG1 under RLS, lists the lids still bound to W, ingests again from lid 999999999999999, and queues an AI reply in each conversation.

After AG1's RLS DELETE, the only lid bound to W was 888888888888888, and the next message from lid 999999999999999 resolved to a NEW contact (f377c287-...), not W. Apply the same change to the watchdog copy, so the send path, the redrive and reply-address share one rule. Regression tests: an @lid not matching any of the contact's lids returns null; the existing test 'a última recebida em @lid também vale' supplies the matching lid; and a watchdog test asserts the redrive falls back to the contact's wa_lid after the extra is removed.

likelihood.reason: It requires a contact with two or more extras where the removed extra was the last to write through an @lid chat, plus an outbound before the customer writes again. No attacker action is needed beyond a routine removal.

impact.reason: The customer's conversation content (AI, follow-up, scheduled and human replies) goes to a WhatsApp account that the operator explicitly detached and that the CRM now treats as a separate contact, while the screen tells the operator replies go to the principal. Removing a malicious extra does not cut off its delivery.

title: Web Push subscriptions survive sign-out, sign-out-everywhere and password reset, and the next user of the browser cannot rebind them, so org conversation previews keep reaching a signed-out or shared browser
description: This diff turns Web Push on by default: completar_par_vapid generates the VAPID pair on install and on every update. Every signed-in page load registers the browser's push subscription in push_subscriptions, bound to (organization, user) by the unique endpoint (AppShell → useInboundMessageAlerts → syncPushSubscription → PUT /api/v1/notifications/push). None of the session-ending paths touches that binding: the signOut action, the signOutEverywhere action ('Sair de todos os dispositivos', scope global), updatePassword and the client AuthProvider.signOut. They only end the Supabase session and delete the active_org cookie. The DELETE /api/v1/notifications/push route has no caller in app, lib, hooks or components. The source also has no Clear-Site-Data header, no serviceWorker unregister and no pushManager unsubscribe outside the VAPID key mismatch branch. The only service worker is /notify-sw.js with scope '/'. When a different person signs in on the same browser profile, syncPushSubscription reuses the existing browser subscription and PUTs the same endpoint. That person can be a shared reception or clinic desk user, or a member of another tenant on the same install. The push_subscriptions_own policy (USING user_id = auth.uid()) makes the PostgREST upsert ON CONFLICT (endpoint) DO UPDATE fail with 42501. The route turns that into a 500 and the client ignores the response, so the endpoint stays bound to the previous user's org. For message.received, the event-log handler sends a payload with the contact label (name or formatted phone) as title, up to 140 characters of the message text as body, and a signed avatar URL valid for 300 s. message.group_received and Central notices are sent the same way. Each goes to every subscription of an active member who can see the conversation. notify-sw.js suppresses the notification only when a window of the origin is visible. Otherwise it calls showNotification without any session check. A lost or shared device that the owner signed out remotely therefore keeps receiving the previews whenever the browser runs with no visible CRM tab. Verifier's bounded check (agents/verifier-onda2/artifacts/evidence/push-rebind.log, throwaway Postgres 16 with the Supabase prelude and baseline.sql) used dummy users A (agent, org X), C (agent, org X) and B (agent, org Y). A's upsert succeeded. B's and C's upserts of the same endpoint failed with 42501 'new row violates row-level security policy (USING expression)'. B's DELETE-route equivalent removed 0 rows. The service-role delivery query of enviarAosUsuarios (organization X, user A) still returned the row. The installed schema has 0 triggers on push_subscriptions and 0 public/auth functions referencing it. Revoked members are already handled by removerPushDoMembro and the active-member filter; this candidate covers session invalidation and the next user of a browser only. Not observed locally because no browser is available: that the browser keeps the PushSubscription and service worker after the cookie-only sign-out, and that a push received afterwards is displayed. Fix direction: before the sign-out action, the client should getSubscription, DELETE /api/v1/notifications/push for that endpoint, then call unsubscribe(). signOutEverywhere and updatePassword should delete all push_subscriptions rows of the user with the service role. The PUT should handle an endpoint held by another user by deleting the old binding with the service role when the caller presents the same p256dh/auth keys. The 'alerts off' switch should also unsubscribe.
claimed_root_cause: The push_subscriptions binding is a long-lived delivery credential tied to (organization, user). At send time it is checked only against active membership and conversation visibility, never against a live session. No session-ending path revokes it, neither on the server (row delete) nor in the browser (PushSubscription.unsubscribe). The endpoint-unique upsert under the user_id = auth.uid() policy also stops the next signed-in user from replacing the binding, so the previous user's org previews keep flowing to that browser.

trace.description: On every signed-in load (AppShell → useInboundMessageAlerts.ts:116), the browser's existing push subscription is reused (or created) and its endpoint is PUT to the server
Cookie-session upsert with onConflict 'endpoint' binds the endpoint to organization_id = active org and user_id = current user

Sign-out only ends the Supabase session and deletes the active_org cookie. The push row and the browser subscription are untouched; the same holds for signOutEverywhere.ts:17 (scope global) and updatePassword.ts:111

The next user's PUT of the same endpoint reaches ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on a row whose user_id is not auth.uid(). RLS raises 42501, the route returns 500 (route.ts:90) and the client ignores it, so the endpoint stays bound to the previous user's org
For message.received the handler builds a payload with the contact label as title, the message preview as body and a signed avatar URL, then sends it to everyone who can see the conversation
Selects subscriptions only by organization_id and active-member user_id; there is no session binding
webpush.sendNotification sends the preview to the stale endpoint
The service worker shows the contact label and preview in the OS tray or lock screen whenever no window of the origin is visible, without any session check

evidence.description: The only cleanup on sign-out is store.delete('active_org'); there is no push subscription delete
'Sair de todos os dispositivos' calls only auth.signOut({scope:'global'}); the user's push_subscriptions rows remain
Password reset ends with a plain auth.signOut(); push rows remain
Client signOut only resets realtime auth before the server action; there is no pushManager unsubscribe
The DELETE handler exists, but nothing in app, lib, hooks or components calls it
Any upsert error other than PGRST205, including the 42501 RLS violation, is returned as a 500 that push_client.ts:52 never inspects
endpoint text not null unique: one browser endpoint can be bound to only one (org, user), and only that user can update it under RLS
The only unsubscribe in the client is for a VAPID key mismatch, never for a user change or sign-out
The single service worker /notify-sw.js is registered at scope '/'; no code unregisters it

removerPushDoMembro documents the intended invariant (a device of someone who lost access must not keep getting previews on its lock screen), but it is only called from the revoke route (team/[user_id]/revoke/route.ts:90)
Turning alerts off tells the user 'Este navegador não vai mais avisar na bandeja', but it only sets a localStorage flag that the service worker never reads
The sign-out-everywhere dialog promises that every device must log in again, yet push delivery to those devices continues
completar_par_vapid creates the VAPID pair on install (install.sh:1808) and on every update (update.sh:84), so the push path is live by default after this diff
The only suppression condition is a visible window of the origin; a browser with no visible CRM tab displays every push

blockers: No browser is available in the sandbox, so two facts were not observed: that a Chromium or Firefox PushSubscription and the /notify-sw.js registration survive the server-action sign-out (cookie deletion only, no Clear-Site-Data), and that a push received afterwards is displayed by the service worker.

Delivery from the server to a real browser goes through the browser vendor's push service (FCM or Mozilla autopush), which is external and unreachable offline. Local evidence stops at the service-role delivery query still returning the stale binding, plus the hunter's recorder showing webpush.sendNotification called for it.
